title: Charles III of Lorraine to the comte de Vaudémont, Nancy, 18 June 1592, BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (DECODE R9449)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3621 no. 97, fol. 109 (Gallica btv1b52524472n, canvas 227; DECODE R9449)

plaintext.source: A contemporary 'Coppie' with the cipher left in; DECODE R9449 non-decrypted; no. 22 in the same volume is a plaintext decipherment of other (January) letters, with no cipher, so no crib.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, per-line crops at about 1.5x native (lc/), after shear deskew -0.031
transcription.notes: _check_profile.py --measure --drop-first gives 1,153 tokens / 94 distinct because it counts the 34 inline clear words in [[ ]] and 10 punctuation marks; excluding those gives 1,109 cipher tokens (1,071 letter symbols in 44 forms + 38 nomenclator figures in 14 values), as NOTES states. About a quarter of glyph identifications are still wrong (merge-control calibration), so the transcription is the limit.

system.summary: Letter substitution in ordinary cursive letterforms and their barred, dotted or capital variants, with modest homophony, plus numeric nomenclator figures (13-146) for names and words.

diacritics.note: Crossbar, overbar and dots on a letterform make a distinct cipher symbol.

system.sibling_key: Four 1592 key sheets in the Nevers key book fr. 3995 (ff. 32, 83-84, 98, 103) examined and eliminated; no Lorraine key on DECODE, Cryptiana or in print. None used.
system.notes: per_letter is the 44-symbol key in ct/no97_solution.txt; with a quarter of glyph identifications wrong, some homophones may be transcription splits. Coincidence statistics put the system between monoalphabetic and fully homophonic.

prior_solution.where: DECODE R9449 'Non-decrypted'; no key in DECODE, Tomokiyo's Cryptiana, HistoCrypt proceedings, the BnF notices or Lepage 1864.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution: the work was done and committed by GitHub user aryasn2026 (git author of all three commits) and merged as pull request #4 after review (docs/lorraine1592.html). What the contributor did beyond running the model is not recorded. The NOTES ask the user to verify the DECODE queries, the Charles II/III identification and every transcription.

solution.what: Verify step: looked for the ciphered originals of the January intercepts in fr. 3621; no. 22 is a plaintext decipherment only, no cipher in the volume to pair it with.
Key sought in DECODE (8 records for fr. 3621), Cryptiana, HistoCrypt, BnF notices, Lepage 1864: none published; other Lorraine keys are different systems.
Four 1592 key sheets in fr. 3995 whose DECODE profile matched (ff. 32, 83-84, 98, 103) fetched and eliminated on their own evidence.
Shear-deskew line finder segments 20 lines / 1,114 glyphs; clear text of nos. 22 and 97 transcribed; unsupervised shape clustering of the glyphs.
Homophonic annealer (solve.py) against a Montaigne 4-gram model on the clustered glyphs: -2.78/char against -1.85 for real French.
Glyphs recognised as ordinary cursive letterforms and transcribed by eye from 42 half-line crops: 1,071 letter symbols in 44 forms and 38 figures (ct/no97_eye.txt).
Old annealer on a control with a known key recovers only 37-56% (true key -1.62 vs found -2.64): the search, not the model, had failed.
Steepest-ascent iterated local search (search.py) recovers known keys at 98.7-99.6%; free nulls and degenerate all-e keys identified as traps and blocked.
Search on the manuscript: key stable across seeds and under a locked crib, -2.10/char; words produced unprompted (munitions, prisonniers, secours, quartiers, conserver la plaine).
Eight-symbol group reading 'chasteau' at lines 15 and 19, with Chasteauvillain twice in the clear on the page; one symbol short (chasteauilains), so eight letters secure and six probable.
Null test: same pipeline on five shuffled ciphertexts gives 0-3 distinct French words of 6+ letters (mean 1.2) against 33 for the manuscript.
Noise and systematic-merge controls: the -2.10 score matches 6-12 merged glyph pairs, i.e. about 65-75% of letters correct; the transcription limits the reading.

outcome.fraction_read_source: ct/no97_eye.txt with the key in ct/no97_solution.txt: cipher tokens (letter symbols + figures; [[clear]] words and punctuation excluded); every letter symbol has a key value, the 38 figure tokens are unread

gaps.item: Connective text between secure words: about a quarter of the glyph identifications in ct/no97_eye.txt are wrong
gaps.detail: Re-reading the 42 crops in lc/ with the key in hand, correcting barred, dotted and capital variants, was proposed and not done (NOTES section 6, ct/no97_reading.md section 6).
No key survives; values only from context or a second letter in the same cipher.

outcome.notes: fraction_read counts symbols given a value (1,071/1,109); fraction_coherent is an estimate from the merge controls (65-75% of letters correct), not a measurement, and it is the figure the read bar uses. NOTES.md has no '## Remaining gaps' or '## Escalation' section; the gaps above are taken from NOTES section 6 and ct/no97_reading.md section 6. Contributed by aryasn2026 (PR #4).
